channel.title: AIBuilder Marketplace — new honest reviews
channel.description: Hand-researched, honest software reviews: real pricing, the honest knock, who should skip it. No hype, no invented numbers.

item.title: HubSpot Review (2026): Per-Seat Pricing & the Catch
item.description: HubSpot: Free is $0 for up to 2 users and 1,000 marketing contacts, with no time limit. Three numbers on this pricing page are not what they look like.

item.title: Qoyod Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Qoyod: Billed in Saudi riyal, which is pegged to the dollar at 3.75. The entry tier does not do the thing the product is sold on.

item.title: Attribuly Review (2026): Free Tier & the Catch
item.description: Attribuly: A free plan that covers the first $1,000 of recovered email revenue, then Capture at $450 a month and Recapture at $500.

item.title: AutoWrite Review (2026): Free Tier & the Catch
item.description: AutoWrite: A free plan is available; the listing showed no paid tiers and no prices at the time of reading. Not one merchant has publicly reported using it.

item.title: GeoStock Review (2026): Trial Terms, Price & Limits
item.description: GeoStock: From $9.99 a month, with a free trial. Know what this is before you buy it: despite the name it is a storefront widget, not an inventory system.

item.title: HelpCenter Review (2026): Trial Terms, Price & Limits
item.description: HelpCenter: Paid runs Basic $5.99, Standard $19.99 and Advanced $49.99 a month. The free tier is the hook and the FAQ builder is the reason people stay.

item.title: Securify Review (2026): Free Tier & the Catch
item.description: Securify: Free plan available with a free trial on the paid tiers. Blocking by country and IP is a blunt instrument and it cuts both ways.

item.title: Atlas AI Store Builder Review (2026): Price & Limits
item.description: Atlas AI Store Builder: The listing says “Free to install”, but that is the development-store tier. The meter runs on your success, not your usage.

item.title: Unleashed Software Review (2026): Real Pricing, Real Limits
item.description: Unleashed Software: Unleashed Core is $399 a month, or $4,389 a year which the page itself puts at $366 equivalent monthly.

item.title: Cloro Review (2026): What the Meter Really Costs
item.description: Cloro: Free is $0 for 500 credits a month, one concurrent job and one seat. The free tier is a sampler, not a trial of the real thing.

item.title: Seller Investigators Review (2026): Price & Limits
item.description: Seller Investigators: One number, and it is the whole model. Contingency pricing is the honest kind — you pay only out of money that arrived.

item.title: ADP Review (2026): No Public Price — What We Found
item.description: ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site. The quote-only posture is normal in payroll.

item.title: Aplos Review (2026): From $79/mo, and the Catch
item.description: Aplos — Three published tiers, billed monthly: Lite at $79/month, then $129, then $229. The headline you will see first is not the price you will pay.

item.title: CloudTask Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: CloudTask: The Hiring Membership is $299/month with no contract and cancel-anytime. What you will actually spend is the all-in monthly rate per hire.

item.title: Digit Review (2026): From $400/mo, and the Catch
item.description: Digit: Starter $400/month including 5 users, Growth $750 including 10, Professional $1,300 including 15. The tier price is a floor, not a ceiling.

item.title: Parim Review (2026): Real Pricing, Real Limits
item.description: Parim: The page says pricing starts from £47 per month with unlimited users on every plan. Unlimited users sounds like the generous part, and it is.

item.title: Planday Review (2026): Per-Seat Pricing & the Catch
item.description: Planday: Starter is €2.99 per user per month with a 5-user minimum. The €25 monthly platform fee on Plus is the line most comparisons miss.

item.title: respond.io Review (2026): From $79/mo, and the Catch
item.description: respond.io — Four tiers, billed on monthly active contacts rather than seats: Starter $79/month, Growth $159, Advanced $279, and Enterprise on quote.

item.title: Flatpay Review (2026): Real Pricing, Real Limits
item.description: Flatpay: £995 for mobile POS, £1,495 for POS Pro and £2,495 for POS Premium. “Zero monthly fees” is the headline, and there genuinely is no subscription.

item.title: Answering Service Care Review (2026): Price & Limits
item.description: Answering Service Care: $161, $296 and $575 for the three larger plans. Do the arithmetic before you pick a tier, because their own page does not.

item.title: Drip Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Drip — One ladder, no tiers: you drag a slider to your list size and Drip prints a monthly price. The word “unlimited” quietly expires.

item.title: Nouswise Review (2026): What the Meter Really Costs
item.description: Nouswise: Four tiers, billed monthly. Their own site does not agree with itself about what this costs, and we have now checked that twice.

item.title: Quartile Review (2026): No Public Price — What We Found
item.description: Quartile: Budget for this one from a written quote, because nothing else exists. Everything about the sales motion here is a conversation.

item.title: Remote People Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Remote People: US PEO from $99 per employee a month and US payroll from $29. The monthly rates are the cheapest we have on file for this category.

item.title: Signal House Review (2026): What the Meter Really Costs
item.description: Signal House: Usage-based, no platform subscription. The product is sold as an SMS and Voice API and the pricing page publishes no voice rate at all.

item.title: accessiBe Review (2026): From $490/yr, and the Catch
item.description: accessiBe: Micro $490/year up to 5,000 visits a month, Growth $1,490/year up to 30,000, Scale $3,990/year up to 100,000.

item.title: Piktochart Review (2026): Free Tier & the Catch
item.description: Piktochart: Free is $0, Pro is $15 per member per month billed monthly or $10 billed annually, Business is $20 monthly or $17 billed annually.

item.title: BidX Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: BidX: €295 for the default report, custom reports quote-only. The number that decides your bill is the one number the page does not print.

item.title: Pippit Review (2026): Free Tier, Then €9/mo
item.description: Pippit: On monthly billing Starter is €9/mo against a €15 list price. The meter is credits per attempt, not per usable result.

item.title: Salesflow Review (2026): Per-Seat Pricing & the Catch
item.description: Salesflow: Their own pricing page returns a 403 to us. The per-seat price falls steeply with team size — roughly $79 alone against $29.98 at fifty seats.
